about: The client model and what binds a code to the client that asked for it (ADR 0021, "The client declaration"; REQ-AUTHN-002 to 004, REQ-AUTHN-062, REQ-AUTHN-102 to 111, REQ-CLIENT-005, REQ-CLIENT-020, REQ-CLIENT-050, REQ-CLIENT-051). v1 declares a client with a kind (public, confidential, exchange), a PKCE rule per client and registered redirects; v2 keeps the model and narrows it: PKCE with S256 for every client, the nonce in place of it only for a confidential client that says so, the profile of a public client closed to browser and native, and every contradiction refused when the file loads. Names are made up (example.org). actors/store is held to "config"; actors/session is held to "authorize", "redirects" and "token". Not in these tables: the answer to a missing code_verifier is invalid_request in v2 where v1 said invalid_grant (an open question for the maintainer, not a vector), and what v1's sign_in_exchange, signed_out, display_name, harness and backchannel_logout_uri become (REQ-SESS-020, #779, #780: no record decides them yet).

config.about: What the loader takes as one client's declaration. The client is named app; client is the YAML mapping as written (JSON is YAML), and the loader reads it with no other document. accepted clients load. refused ones fail at the field named by error's path, with its words, and no value in the message. A refusal that comes from the schema before the loader has other words; the loader's words are the ones held here, and the verdict is the same (REQ-DATA-038).

authorize.about: What session does with an authorization request, for each way of declaring a client. A setup is a client as the loader stored it (secret is whether it names one), with the redirect it registered and the one its request presents. A request is the PKCE part of an authorization request: challenge is a token the test makes a value of (valid is the S256 of the verifier, short and long are 42 and 44 characters of the alphabet, padded is a valid one ending in =, outside is one with a character outside base64url, absent is none) and method is the code_challenge_method as sent (absent is none); nonce is valid for ten characters, seven for seven, eight for exactly eight, spaces for sixty spaces, and absent for none. outcome is begins (the sign-in goes to the upstream), or the error that goes to the client's redirect, with the closed reason the audit record gives (pkce, nonce), or page for a request that cannot be redirected (an exchange client is no client of a person's code). A request that sends a challenge or a method is a PKCE request whatever the setup says (REQ-AUTHN-105).

redirects.about: Whether a redirect_uri that an authorization request presents is one the client registered (REQ-AUTHN-003, REQ-AUTHN-004; RFC 6749 section 3.1.2.3, RFC 8252 sections 7.3 and 8.3, RFC 9700 section 4.1). registered is the client's list. A match is the exact string, with one exception: an http redirect registered on a loopback IP literal without a port matches any port from 1 to 65535 of the same address, path and query. environment is the boundary's (development when left out). A redirect that does not match is a page, never a redirect to the presented address. kinds and profile name the client; every kind that signs a person in is held to the same rule.

token.about: What the token endpoint does with the PKCE part of a code request. mode is how the code was bound when it was issued: s256 (a challenge, and verifier is what the client holds) or nonce (no challenge, a confidential client set to the nonce). verifier is what the request presents: right (the one the challenge was made from), wrong (another valid one), plain (the challenge itself, which is what a plain-method client would send), none, or any (a valid one, for a code bound by the nonce). outcome is ok or the error. A code that was issued without a challenge is redeemed only while its client is still set to the nonce (REQ-AUTHN-107). A refusal spends nothing: the right request that follows it still works (REQ-AUTHN-106). A missing verifier for an s256 code is not here: v2 says invalid_request, v1 said invalid_grant.
